title: The Concept Allocation Zone: Tracking How Concepts Form Across Transformer Depth
abstract: arXiv:2605.24856v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Concept formation in transformer language models is a depth-extended process, not a single-layer event: a concept becomes separable across one or more contiguous regions of the residual stream - its Concept Allocation Zone (CAZ). A CAZ is not a concept but the depth segment where the model organizes its geometry to make one separable - concepts may share a CAZ, and typically span multiple across depth; the companion GEM paper shows the separating direction continues to rotate within a CAZ before stabilizing past its boundary. We formalize the CAZ through three layer-wise metrics - Separation, Concept Coherence, and Concept Velocity - with automated boundary detection that applies no significance threshold to CAZ membership (every segment is a CAZ; "strong" vs. "gentle" is score, never a binary cut). translated_title: 概念分配区：追踪概念如何跨越Transformer深度形成
translated_abstract: 概念形成在Transformer语言模型中是一个深度扩展的过程，而非单层事件：一个概念在一个或多个残差流的连续区域内变得可分离——该区域称为其概念分配区（CAZ）。CAZ不是概念本身，而是模型组织其几何结构以使概念可分离的深度段——概念可能共享CAZ，并通常跨越多个深度段；配套的GEM论文表明，分离方向在CAZ内部持续旋转，直到越过其边界后才稳定。我们通过三个逐层指标——分离度、概念连贯性和概念速度——来形式化CAZ，并采用自动边界检测，该检测不对CAZ成员资格施加显著性阈值（每个段都是CAZ；“强”与“温和”是分数，而非二元划分）。跨35个模型、8个架构家族和7个概念的实证验证表明，分离曲线S(l)经常是多模态的。
tldr: 本文提出了“概念分配区”概念，表明Transformer中概念形成是跨深度的连续过程，并通过三个指标和自动边界检测实现了对概念形成位置和过程的精确追踪。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "Concept Allocation Zone" (CAZ), showing that concept formation in Transformers is a depth-extended process, and provides three metrics with automated boundary detection to precisely track where and how concepts form across layers.
